item.title: Fed’s Goolsbee says he sees no clear path back to 2% inflation
item.description:
Goolsbee’s comments on inflation, interest rates and AI investment crossed the wires.

  • What is happening with services inflation is important in understanding whether price pressures stem from demand or things like energy costs.
  • Inflation has proven to be far more persistent than was thought in 2025, and data center demand and AI-related wealth impact is adding to it.
  • The steepness of the interest-rate path will be rooted in whether “borderline disturbingly high” inflation is seen returning to Fed’s 2% target.
  • Does not see at this point that inflation is on the path back to 2%. It is not just coming from oil and tariff shocks, but a sizable demand component.
  • Is not concerned about wages pressuring inflation at this point.
  • It has not been good news on inflation for the past few months.
  • Anthropic’s IPO raises the question of how stockholders will use that wealth. It could have a macroeconomic impact.
  • Artificial intelligence is influencing today’s economy through wealth impacts and investment.
  • There is widespread acknowledgment among businesses that costs are up, particularly among firms in construction or competing with data centers for components.
  • Is not sure if fallout from US midterm elections will include a slowdown in data-center buildout or have a lasting impact on equity prices.
  • More openness about monetary policy has been productive for the Fed and the world.
  • Consumer spending has been pretty broad-based, financed mostly out of income growth.
  • There is a high risk that economy’s capacity cannot handle the current “pig-through-the-python” level of business investment without overheating.
  • Not clear how financial sector would be impacted if there is a major correction in equities related to AI.

Analysis

The takeaway is hawkish. Goolsbee sees a sizable demand component to inflation, which makes it harder for the Fed to look through the recent price pressure. Businesses are already reporting higher costs where they compete with data centers for components, and he sees a risk that the economy has trouble absorbing the current pace of investment without overheating.

Services inflation is the barometer to watch. If it stays sticky even as energy pressures ease, that would strengthen the case that demand is keeping inflation elevated and give the Fed more reason to tighten. If services inflation cools, the case for a steeper rate path weakens.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: AUDUSD moves to a new low. Price action is ping ponging down and up and back down again.
item.description:
Australia’s October jobs report was considerably weaker than expected. Employment fell 43,500 against the 25,500 gain expected in our preview, and the unemployment rate rose to 4.9% versus 4.7% expected. September’s job loss was revised to 36,400 from 39,300, putting the two-month decline at nearly 80,000 jobs, the biggest in five years.

Part-time jobs accounted for most of the decline

  • Full-time employment fell 2,900. Part-time employment fell 40,600.
  • Participation fell to 66.6% from 66.8%, while the number of unemployed people still rose by 17,800. Hours worked fell 0.2%.
  • Youth unemployment rose to 11.3% from 11.1%, also the highest since October 2021.

The rise in unemployment alongside a drop in participation is the detail that stands out. A smaller share of Australians were working or looking for work, and even with that decline in participation, more people were unemployed. The ABS’s smoothed trend measure still showed a modest gain of 7,200 jobs, but trend unemployment also rose, to 4.8%.

The RBA has more reason to pause

The RBA raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% earlier this month and warned that inflation would stay elevated for longer. The jobs report strengthens the case for a hold on December 8. Reuters reported that traders unwound bets on further hikes and priced in roughly 45 basis points of easing by the end of 2027, about double what they had priced before the release

Technically, the price moved lower  but bounced before reversing to a new low.

The AUDUSD initially fell sharply from 0.67202 to near 0.6660 after the weaker-than-expected Australian jobs report. Buyers came back in and erased nearly the entire decline, taking the pair back toward the Asian session high at 0.6720 early in North American trading.

That rebound did not last. As U.S. stocks reversed their early gains, traders turned their attention back to U.S. inflation concerns and still-solid jobs data. Sellers took control again, retracing the entire bounce and extending the move to a new session low at 0.66562. The pair is trading at 0.66624 as the North American session winds down.

The 200-week moving average is the barometer

The session low at 0.66562 dipped just below the 200-week moving average at 0.66575. The price is back above it for now, putting the focus on where the pair closes the week. A weekly close below 0.66575 would give sellers more control and increase the potential for further downside.

If buyers can hold above that moving average and build on the bounce, the 100-week moving average at 0.67043 is the first key topside target. Getting back above it would give buyers more room to make a run at the session high near 0.6720.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: No relief for US stocks. Major indices trade to new lows
item.description:
US stocks are getting no relief. The Dow is down more than 1,000 points, the Nasdaq 100 is off more than 2%, and the Russell 2000 is down nearly 2%. The selling is broad, and the early lift from anticipation of Anthropic’s first trade has faded.

Inflation keeps the pressure on stocks

The concern for stocks is that persistent inflation could keep the Fed leaning toward tighter policy even as the risks to growth increase. Higher borrowing costs can weigh on spending and investment, while higher rates make it harder for investors to justify elevated valuations. That is a difficult combination for stocks, particularly when investors are already questioning how much growth they are willing to pay for.

Anthropic’s IPO adds to the pressure

Anthropic’s debut gave the broader market a lift early, but that bid did not hold. The focus now shifts to what investors may be selling to make room for the new stock. When an IPO of this size lands in a market already under pressure, the reshuffling can add to the selling in other names. With small caps down nearly as much as the Nasdaq, the weakness extends well beyond the AI trade.

item.title: Canada seeks interim U.S. tariff deal by year-end, CBC reports
item.description:
CBC News reported, citing sources familiar with Thursday’s meeting between Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc and the federal government’s Canada-U.S. economic advisory committee, that Ottawa is aiming for an interim tariff agreement with the Trump administration. CBC News

  • Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada still wants a U.S. deal and is pursuing other trade opportunities. On his latest trip, Canada reached free trade deals with the Philippines and ASEAN and secured greater access to China for Canadian commodities.
  • Carney met with U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China. The discussion ended without a trade breakthrough.
  • Carney told the DealBook Summit on Wednesday that talks had made progress in recent weeks, but the two sides had yet to put anything in writing.
  • Ottawa is seeking relief from Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum, autos and lumber, along with Section 338 tariffs imposed on Canadian goods in August after earlier talks broke down.

Analysis

The year-end target gives CAD traders a date to watch. The first test is whether the two sides can put terms in writing. From there, the scope matters. Relief across steel, aluminum, autos and lumber could ease cost pressure for Canadian exporters and give the Canadian dollar some support. The details to watch are which tariffs come down, by how much and when.

Technically speaking...

Looking at the USDCAD on the hourly chart below, the price today did fall below the 100 hour MA and a swing area in the 1.42198 to 1.42986 area. However, momentum could not be sustained below that key break and the price has pushed higher.  Earlier in the day, the price reached the highest level since April 2025 at 1.43566.  That is the next target with close risk now at the rising 100 hour MA at 1.4302.  Move above 1.43566 and traders will look toward the swing highs from March 19, 2025 and April 1, 2025 at 1.4401 to 1.44145 (not shown). 

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: GBPUSD breaks to a new 2026 low. The daily chart shows room to the downside.
item.description:
The GBPUSD is trading to a new low for 2026 as inflation concerns push the greenback higher. The move lower gathered momentum after sellers leaned against resistance on the hourly chart. On the daily chart, the break below a key floor gives sellers room to probe lower.

Daily chart. The break below the floor opens the door toward 1.3000.

The GBPUSD is breaking below the daily swing area between 1.31386 and 1.31786. The move also takes the price further away from 1.31926, the 38.2% retracement of the rally from the January 2025 low.

The lower edge of the old floor near 1.3139 is the first barometer on a bounce. If the price stays below it, sellers keep the downside bias. A move back into the swing area would take some of the momentum out of the break. Buyers would then need to work through the upper end of the area and get back above 1.31926 to give themselves more breathing room.

On the downside, the next daily swing area comes in between 1.2998 and 1.3046. The top of that area at 1.3046 is the first target. Below that, the focus shifts toward 1.2998 and then 1.29838, the 50% midpoint of the rally from the January 2025 low.

Hourly chart. Sellers leaned against 1.3171 and pushed to new lows.

Drilling down to the hourly chart above, the rebound off the earlier low stalled near 1.3171, the lower edge of a swing area that extends to 1.31808. The 100-hour moving average sits within that area near 1.31797, adding to the resistance.

Sellers leaned against the bottom of the area and were rewarded with a push to fresh lows. That gives traders a sequence to watch on the next bounce. A move above 1.3171 would be the first sign that buyers are making a play. Getting and staying above the 100-hour moving average and 1.31808 would give that move more credibility.

For now, the daily chart shows where the price has room to go, and the hourly chart shows where sellers can define their risk. With the pair making new lows for the year, the burden of proof remains on the buyers.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Trump weighs another strike on Iran as Hormuz shipping risks mount. Returns to Washington after overseas trip.
item.description:
Geopolitics is building as President Trump is heading back to Washington after wrapping up talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen. Ukraine was a focus coming out of the meetings. 

Of course Iran is also a continued focus.  

With Xi, Iran, Hormuz, Taiwan and trade.

Trump said he and Xi agreed that Iran should fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz and should not acquire a nuclear weapon. Trump also urged China to help end the war in Ukraine. Beijing’s readout emphasized Taiwan and Xi’s call for better communication on trade and economic issues.

With Putin, a possible path to ending the Ukraine war.

Ukraine came up in Trump’s one-on-one with Putin and again in the three-way talks. Afterward, US envoy Jared Kushner said Russia was comfortable with the idea of NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine. Putin separately ruled out direct talks with Kyiv, citing Ukraine’s strike on the Kerch Bridge

With all three, nuclear risks and energy supplies.

The leaders agreed to hold talks on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. They also called for increasing supplies of refined petroleum products and keeping energy flows stable. The joint declaration gave no production targets or timeline and made no mention of either war.

Trump is weighing his options on Iran

US President Donald Trump is considering another strike on Iran, Israel’s Channel 12 reported, citing an Israeli source. The broadcaster said Trump is in no rush to make a decision and that any strike would be carried out in cooperation with Israel. It said potential targets could include nuclear facilities, infrastructure and senior officials.

Hormuz is the immediate focus for oil traders

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Wednesday saw by far the largest flow out of the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, i24NEWS, citing unnamed sources, reported that Iran had become more aggressive in recent days and was using cruise missiles against ships passing through the strait. The report did not provide details on which vessels were affected or whether they sustained damage.

The Houthis also said on Telegram that they would release a statement at 1:30 p.m. ET about what they described as military operations deep inside Saudi Arabia. The announcement itself offered no details about the operations or any impact on energy infrastructure.

For WTI and Brent, the next thing to watch is whether Wednesday’s larger flow through Hormuz can be sustained. Continued improvement would help ease some of the supply concerns. A renewed slowdown in traffic or confirmed damage to energy infrastructure could put the geopolitical risk premium back in focus.

Kushner says Trump is open to Ukraine security guarantees

On Ukraine, US special envoy Jared Kushner said Trump came away from the Shenzhen meeting believing peace was achievable. Kushner said there had been progress on a postwar economic plan and that Russia had agreed to engage in a multilateral format with European countries. He added that Trump wants Europe alongside him in reaching a deal.

Kushner said Trump was open to an Article 5-style security guarantee for Ukraine, provided it served US interests. Any agreement would still have to spell out what the US and Europe would commit to if Ukraine came under attack again.

Trump sets a Friday news conference

Trump said he was heading back to Washington from China and would hold a White House news conference Friday at noon ET. He said he would also discuss trade deals with Thailand, the Philippines and other countries.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Fed's Goolsbee: Job market is stable, but inflation is "way higher" than Fed's 2% target
item.description:
Comments from Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, a 2027 FOMC voter, crossed the wires on inflation, jobs and consumer demand.

  • The impact of tariffs has been more persistent than expected.
  • The job market is stable, but inflation is “way higher” than the Fed’s 2% target. Consumer demand has been very strong and solid.
  • AI seems promising as a boost to productivity but the day job of the Fed is to determine if the economy is overheating now
  • The job market is stable.
  • The Fed failure has been on inflation.  
  • Changes in immigration policy means the Fed should put less weight on monthly job numbers as a signal about the business cycle.
  • Fed is still looking for evidence AI driven productivity is starting to move beyond the tech sector.
  • Unless AI shows a can increase productivity outside the tech sector, it could prove a flash in the pan.

Analysis

The tone is hawkish. If tariffs are still feeding through to prices, one source of inflation may take longer to fade. At the same time, solid consumer demand gives businesses room to pass along higher costs, and a stable job market gives the Fed room to keep its focus on inflation. For traders, the question heading into December is whether the inflation data make the case for a faster pace of tightening.

Remember the Fed did nothing at the end of October meeting most likely due to the elections in early November.  The minutes of the meeting were more hawkish yesterday. 

In the absence of the election, would the Fed have tightened?  My guess is yes.   So 50 bps in December would get the Fed to what would be the normal progression given the inflation threat.   If the Fed is failing on inflation, do something about it.  

The market is still only implying a small 5.6% chance for a 50 bp hike in December (it has been up at about 10% recently). 

What other Fed officials said this week

  • Christopher Waller, Nov. 18 — Inflation is spreading across more categories, with roughly 70% of core services items running above 3%. He warned that businesses could start treating 3% as normal and made the case for a 50-basis-point hike in December or a clear signal that rates would rise faster in the months ahead.
  • Mary Daly, Nov. 18 — Inflation has been too high for too long, and its path remains uncertain. She described the labor market as stable and said spending was holding up even among lower-income households. images.investinglive.com
  • Alberto Musalem, Nov. 17 — The risks tilt toward inflation staying above 2%. He said several rate increases would likely be needed before spring 2027 and argued that moving sooner could help bring inflation down while expectations are still anchored.
  • Beth Hammack, Nov. 16 — Inflation pressures are worsening, but she still favors slow, steady rate hikes and sees little reason to accelerate the pace at this point.
This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: European stocks close lower. Anthropic opens 34% above its IPO price.
item.description:
European stocks finish lower across the board

As London and European traders head for the exits, the major indices are all lower. Spain’s IBEX 35 led the declines, while the UK’s FTSE 100 and Germany’s DAX each fell a little over 0.9%. Italy’s FTSE MIB held up the best of the group, but still lost 0.46%.

  • German DAX −0.92% to 25,498.90
  • France’s CAC 40 −0.81% to 8,080.74
  • UK FTSE 100 −0.93% to 10,452.68
  • Spain’s IBEX 35 −0.97% to 19,186.20
  • Italy’s FTSE MIB −0.46% to 49,941.24

French yields lead the move higher

European 10-year yields rose across the board, with France leading the way. The French 10-year rose 7.5 basis points to 4.942% (the high for the cycle reached in October extended to 5.142%), while Germany’s rose 4.0 basis points to 3.412% (recent high at 3.653%). That widened the French-German spread by 3.5 basis points to 153 basis points (high at 176 bps).

Elsewhere, Spain’s 10-year rose 5.1 basis points to 3.999%, Italy’s rose 3.1 basis points to 4.489%, and the UK’s rose 2.6 basis points to 5.329%.

Anthropic opens at $111.50. The Dow falls more than 400 points.

Anthropic’s first trade on the Nasdaq came in at $111.50, up $28.50, or 34.3%, from its $83 IPO price. That was also above the earlier $104 indication. The shares traded as high as $115.10 and as low as $109.99, and were at $111.64 as European traders wrapped up their day.

The Nasdaq Composite was up 0.47% and the Nasdaq 100 was up 0.50% at the European close. The gains didn’t carry across the broader market. The Dow was down 442 points, or 0.88%, the Russell 2000 was down 0.59%, and the S&P 500 was just below unchanged, down 0.07%.

U.S. continuing claims jump as Philly Fed new orders slip below zero

Initial jobless claims rose by just 1K to 203K from a revised 202K, above the 197K estimate. The bigger move was in continuing claims, which jumped 70K to 1.763 million from 1.693 million, well above the 1.710 million estimate. The insured unemployment rate held at 1.1%. investinglive.com

The November Philly Fed manufacturing index fell to 6.3 from 20.9, well below the 20.0 estimate and the lowest reading since May. The headline stayed in expansion territory, but new orders fell to −0.4 from 4.3. Shipments and employment improved, while the prices-paid index jumped to 58.2 from 43.2 and prices received rose to 47.0. For the Fed, that’s a familiar mix of softer demand and persistent price pressure.

The Conference Board’s Leading Economic Index fell 0.3% in October after holding steady in September. Fewer building permits drove most of the decline, while the coincident index, which tracks current activity, was unchanged.

U.S. yields climb, led by the short end

Despite the softer data, Treasury yields were higher at the European close, with the bigger moves at the short end. The 2-year rose 3.4 basis points to 4.834%, the 5-year rose 2.7 basis points to 4.911%, and the 10-year rose 1.9 basis points to 5.085%. The 30-year was up 1.4 basis points at 5.426%.

USDJPY presses toward 160. Oil moves higher.

The dollar was mixed. USDJPY rose 0.35% to 159.89 after reaching 159.96, just shy of the 160.00 level. GBPUSD fell 0.25% to 1.3114, and AUDUSD was down 0.49% at 0.6684. EURUSD was little changed at 1.0981 after trading above 1.1000 earlier, while NZDUSD rose 0.31% to 0.5508 and USDCAD slipped 0.16% to 1.4303.

In commodities, WTI crude gained $1.44, or 1.73%, to $84.70, while Brent rose $1.02, or 1.11%, to $92.97.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Poland's Tusk: It doesn't look probable that Russia will be ready to negotiate peace before spring
item.description:
Poland's Tusk has evidently heard something that's dimmed his hopes for real peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine.

He said that it doesn't look probable that Russia will be ready to negotiate on Ukraine before the end of winter. At the same time, Ukraine's governement bonds have had their biggest fall in a month today.

That's a clear indication that the market sees a dimmed chance of peace. It comes after the Putin, Xi and Trump meeting in China this week, where peace was surely discussed.

There have been intense peace discussions for weeks but it doesn't look like there is a path forward as all sides dig in on borders and the post-war military stance. In the meantime, drone warfare continues to advance in the most-awful ways imaginable at the front lines, with a massive human toll.

In terms of markets, oil prices are bouncing today up 1.4% and recouping about half of yesterday's losses. The real pain is in diesel, in part because Russia's refineries have been a major target of Ukraine and that's massively curbed product exports. The IEA doesn't see much scope for improvement until late 2027 and the clock doesn't really start until we get peace.

As of today, Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine has lasted 1,730 days (4 years, 8 months, 26 days). That means it has already lasted 312 days longer than the Soviet Union's entire war against Nazi Germany, from Hitler's invasion in June 1941 to Germany's defeat in May 1945. It's also longer than the entirety of WWI.

WTI is stalling ahead of the September low of $79.62 and that level and the big figure are the ones to watch to the downside.

Hopes for peace in Iran also appear to be dwindling and that's why the upside risks to oil and products are more compelling. Iran also appears to be escalating attacks on energy, using missiles to sink transiting ships rather than disabling them with drones. 

Increasingly, there are economic worries being priced into oil and that's something worth watching as global central banks hike rates.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: AMD shares tumble after Hunterbrook flags China export risks. What about the technicals?
item.description:
Shares of AMD fell about 9% to $482 after a Hunterbrook Media report raised new questions about the company’s exposure to U.S. export controls on China. The stock traded as low as $470.56 before rebounding to around $488. That bounce puts the price back above a key retracement, giving buyers a nearby level to lean against.

Hunterbrook traces updated AMD firmware to a blacklisted Chinese server maker

Hunterbrook found at least six newer versions of AMD’s server startup software in updates published by IEIT Systems after the Chinese server maker was added to the U.S. export blacklist in March 2025. The investigation also found nearly identical firmware at three vendors it linked to IEIT, including Aivres, which AMD lists as a maker of servers built with its Instinct AI accelerators. hntrbrk.com

How the firmware reached IEIT remains an open question. Hunterbrook could not determine who supplied it or whether the transfer was licensed. AMD had asked for more time and had yet to answer the publication’s questions when the report went live. Hunterbrook Capital, the investment firm affiliated with Hunterbrook Media, disclosed that it was short AMD at publication.

AMD’s China exposure comes back into focus

AMD had been viewed as a potential beneficiary of Nvidia’s China troubles. Today’s report puts the focus back on AMD’s own exposure. The company billed $7.75 billion to customers in China and Hong Kong in fiscal 2025, equal to 22.4% of total sales across all products. On the supply side, two joint ventures with China’s Tongfu provide most of AMD’s chip assembly, testing and packaging services.

For the broader chip sector, the question is whether investors start to price in more risk around where advanced chips can be sold and which customers can access them. That’s where the concern could spill over to Nvidia and other chipmakers. For AMD, it brings export licensing and the reach of its AI growth plans back into the discussion.

The selloff breaks the 200-period moving average on the four-hour chart

Before the report, AMD’s rally stalled near the 100-period moving average on the four-hour chart at $554.24. The news sent the price through the 200-period moving average at $526.45. The selling continued through $478.20, the 38.2% retracement of the move up from the early March low, before buyers finally came in at $470.56.

The rebound to around $488 takes the price back above $478.20. That retracement is now the close barometer for buyers and sellers. Stay above it, and buyers have room to extend the rebound. Move back below it, and the focus returns to $470.56. A break of that low would put the next support area in play.

The $422 to $438 swing area is the next downside target

Below today’s low, the next major area on my chart is the old floor between $422 and $438. The rising 200-day moving average at $428.55 sits inside that range, adding to its importance.

Back on November 5, the price fell below both the swing area and the 200-day moving average. That break failed, and the stock snapped back higher as Nvidia’s troubles helped shift attention toward AMD. If sellers get another look at that area, I’ll be watching whether willing buyers show up again and whether they can keep the price above the 200-day moving average.

For now, $478.20 is the level buyers can lean against. On a deeper rebound, $526.45 is the bigger test. Getting back above that four-hour moving average and staying above it would give buyers more control. Until then, sellers still have the advantage on the four-hour chart.

The major indices are swinging with the news

The broader nanosecond the NASDAQ 100 indices move into negative territory giving up their earlier gains help by the AMD news and fears. The indices have since rebounded back into positive territory, but volatility is high. Meanwhile the premarket shares of anthropic are up to a estimated opening price of $107 versus the $83 IPO price set late yesterday.

NOTE: Shares of AMD are also quite well with shares currently trading at $194 down -6.8%. That is bouncing off of the low of $470.56. Nevertheless, the price still remains comfortably below its 200 hour moving average on the 4 hour chart $526.55

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: The mood shifted in a hurry
item.description:
The rally in stocks barely lasted an hour.

The Nasdaq opened up 2% but it's now in negative territory as we await the first trades in Anthropic. The IPO seems to be going well, with pricing indicated at $105 but that hasn't been able to halt the bearishness in the market.

If we end up closing here, this will be the worst week in the US market since April 2025, with the DJIA falling 5%. A particularly ugly move is in AMD, which is down 8.6% after opening strongly higher. That's a nasty outside day.

The fears are that the AI building boom is running out of gas and that there's no more debt to take on. Moreover, the big winners from the boom -- primarily chipmakers -- will see a harsh mean reversion on earnings in the years ahead.

Some investors may also be looking at the macro picture after Stan Druckenmiller's comments this week. The Fed is hiking rates and could be hiking aggressively as the Iran war continues indefinitely and inflation spreads. Other central banks are also tightening.

The fear is that a global coordinated slowdown (or recession) will hit just as the AI spending taps run dry. For the sake of argument, lets say there is a recession in H2 2027. Is that worth freaking out over? I tend to think it's not. It would get inflation under control and the Fed would have 2-300 bps of ammunition to cut rates.

Now it might be way too early to look through that from a trading perspective but long term investors should see that cushion. If the Fed over-tightens, I'd tend to think it brings the pain forward, but also the window of opportunity to buy the dip forward.

All that said, I really don't think this is about the macro picture. There are real concerns about AI disruption and the ROI on all the spending.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: The broader indices are benefiting from the Anthropic enthusiasm, but there is work to do. What next?
item.description:
As the market awaits the first trade in Anthropic, the enthusiasm surrounding the IPO is giving the broader stock indices a boost. The IPO was priced at $83, and the pre-open indication is at $104. That would represent a 25.3% premium to the IPO price if the first trade were to go off at that level.

The gains are welcome after the recent declines, but the technical picture is different across the three major indices. The S&P 500 has already cleared a key barometer. The Nasdaq Composite has bounced from a floor but given back some of that move, while the Nasdaq 100 remains below both its session high and its 200-day moving average.

So what do the buyers need to do to build on the gains?

S&P 500 buyers get back above the 200-day moving average

The S&P 500 has made the most progress around its 200-day moving average. The index has moved back above that level at 7,348.78, giving buyers a nearby level to define their risk.

As long as the price can stay above the moving average, the buyers have an opening to push toward the next key target near 7,507. A move back below 7,348.78 would take away some of the progress made today and give sellers an opening to push back. For now, that moving average is the barometer for the buyers and sellers.

Nasdaq Composite bounces from its floor. The 200-day moving average is still above.

The Nasdaq Composite has moved away from a floor area between 24,206 and 24,425. The rebound took the index to a high of 24,939.62, but it has since pulled back to around 24,584. That puts it closer to the top of the floor area than to the session high.

On the topside, the buyers first need to get back through 24,939.62. Above that, the 200-day moving average at 25,160.52 is the bigger target. Getting above that moving average and staying above it would give buyers a stronger case that they’re taking back control.

On the downside, a move below 24,425 would put the index back inside the floor area. A break below 24,206 would take out the floor and give the sellers more control.

Nasdaq 100 buyers have work to do before testing 28,108.10

The Nasdaq 100 traded as high as 27,749.25 and has since backed off to 27,270.89. Even at the session high, the index was still about 359 points shy of its 200-day moving average at 28,108.10.

The first job for the buyers is to get back to and through the session high. That would put the 200-day moving average back in play. Until the index can get and stay above that moving average, the sellers still hold the better hand from a broader technical perspective.

In the video above, I walk through all three charts and show why the levels matter. For the S&P 500, the question is whether buyers can defend the 200-day moving average they’ve already reclaimed. For the two Nasdaq indices, the first test is whether buyers can recover the session highs and put their own 200-day moving averages within reach.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Walmart continues the relatively upbeat commentary on consumers
item.description:
The US consumer is fine.

That's the takeaway from this week's earnings reports from Target, Home Depot, Lowes and TJ Maxx. Today it was Walmart and it was more of the same and executives described a solid but not spectacular spending environment.

Shares initially opened down 3% but have pared that to 1% on a softer than expected guide but that comes after strength this week from Target and TJX.

Some details:

  • Walmart U.S. comps rose 2.9% ex-fuel, with transactions up 1.5% and average ticket up 1.4%. A year ago it was 4.5%, with ticket up 2.7%, so ticket growth has halved.
  • Drug pricing distorted the comp. Government limits on pricing cut Q3 Walmart U.S. comps by about 125 bps, partly offset by about 60 bps of growth, mainly from GLP-1s. Excluding health and wellness, Walmart U.S. comps rose 3.6%.
  • Full-year guidance is raised to sales growth of 4.9%–5.2% (from 4%–5%) and adjusted EPS of $2.84–$2.89 (from $2.80–$2.87). Shares have been on a tear, climbing 25% since early October and it looks like something better was priced in or this was used as an opportunity to take profits.

On the consumer:

  • CEO John Furner: “I think the words we would use to describe the customer are stable, resilient.” Pressure appeared in April, then softness in June. Q3 showed recovery, with food share gains and better response to rollbacks.
  • On the holidays, Furner said “we expect a strong holiday season”, and turkey sales are up about 1 million units year over year this month.

Inflation:

  • Food inflation is tame. Furner said grocery inflation ran between 1% and 2% in the quarter, which he called low to normal historically, helped by lapping last year’s egg and dairy spikes.
  • On where it goes next, Furner said “As far as looking ahead, it is hard to call.” He tied it to transportation and input costs.
  • The 26-item holiday meal basket is down about 12% for identical items versus last year, at just over $3.50 per person.
  • Rollbacks (Walmart’s temporary price cuts) are coming down from their peak. There were about 11,000 at the end of Q2 and about 7,700 at the end of Q3, against a normal range of 5,000–5,500.

International:

  • In Canada, net sales rose 6.2% in constant currency and comparable sales rose 6.4%, with growth across categories and strong momentum in food. That echoes what TJX said, but it's tough to tell what's market share and what's consumer health.
  • Walmex, Walmart’s Mexican unit, reported back on October 27. Same-store sales in Mexico rose 1.7%, driven by a 1.6% increase in ticket size and broadly flat traffic. Traffic is flat and the gain is roughly in line with inflation, so the consumer there is just treading water.
  • China was the standout: net sales grew 28.5% in constant currency and comparable sales rose 14.3%, with e-commerce up 31%. Online now accounts for 53% of sales there.

Overall, all the major retailers reporting this week describe the same consumer: more trips and more units, with ticket growth slowing. There's no real sign of a change or extreme K-shape in their data.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: USDCAD sellers make a play after a new high for the year
item.description:
A new high for the year, followed by a rotation lower

The USDCAD has been trending higher since bottoming at 1.3929 in early November. The move to the upside continued in the Asian session today, with the price reaching a new high for the year at 1.43566 (see chart below). That was the highest level going back to April 2025. However, the buyers could not keep the momentum going, and the price rotated back down toward the 100-hour moving average.

That moving average has been a good barometer for the buyers on the way up. The price moved above it on November 5 near 1.3971. On Tuesday, the price came back down to test it near 1.4270, and willing buyers leaned against the level. They could define and limit their risk against the moving average, and the bounce from that test ultimately led to today’s new high.

Sellers are making a play. Can they keep it going?

In the last few hours, the price has traded below the 100-hour moving average, now at 1.4298. That tips the short-term bias in favor of the sellers, but there is more work to do. The moving average is near the top of a swing area between 1.42918 and 1.42990. The sellers need to get and stay below the lower end of that area to give them the go-ahead to push lower.

If they can do that, Tuesday’s low near 1.4270 would be the first target. Remember, that was where buyers leaned against the 100-hour moving average and started the move to today’s high. If the price gets through that low, the rising 200-hour moving average at 1.4248 would be the next target to get to and through.

On the flip side, if the sellers can’t keep the price below the swing area and the pair moves back above 1.42990, the break below the 100-hour moving average starts to look like a failed break. That would give buyers an opening to make another run toward 1.43566.

The 200-hour moving average is the bigger test

The price has been above the 200-hour moving average since early November. Getting below the 100-hour moving average gives the sellers a shot. Getting and staying below the 200-hour moving average would give them more control.

On a break below 1.4248, I would look toward the next swing area between 1.41922 and 1.42040. The 38.2% retracement of the move up from 1.3929 to 1.43566 comes in at 1.41933, within that area. That gives buyers another level to lean against if the correction gets that far.

For now, the close risk for sellers is back above 1.42990. On the downside, 1.42918 is the first level sellers need to get through. How the price behaves there will tell us whether they have enough momentum to take a run at the 200-hour moving average.

Trading education. What gives a moving average break more weight?

When a moving average has held on a pullback, I pay attention the next time the price comes back to it. On Tuesday, buyers leaned against the 100-hour moving average near 1.4270. They could define and limit their risk against that level, and the bounce eventually led to a new high for the year. Today, the price moved below that same moving average. That gives sellers a reason to make a play. The next question is whether they can keep the price below it.

This is where the swing area helps. With the 100-hour moving average near the top of the 1.42918–1.42990 area, a move below the average still leaves support at 1.42918. If the price gets below that lower level and then stalls on a bounce back toward it, sellers have a level to lean against and a downside target at Tuesday’s low. If the price instead moves back above 1.42990 and holds, the break starts to look like a failed break, and the reason for leaning short weakens.

Work through the levels one at a time. The break of the 100-hour moving average gives sellers an opening. A break of the swing area gives them room to extend. Getting and staying below the 200-hour moving average would be the next sign that sellers are taking more control.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Bitcoin buyers make a play off swing area support. What do buyers have to do to increase upside potential?
item.description:
Buyers lean against the four-hour swing area

Bitcoin fell to a low of $61,947 on Sunday, November 15 and bounced but the bounce was somewhat modest to $66069 before sellers returned.  Those sellers took the price back to the Sunday low, and nearly matched it on late  Wednesday. However, the price decline once again ran into willing buyers within the four-hour swing area floor between $61,183 and $62,470 (see red numbered circles on the chart below).

That second test gave buyers another opportunity to lean against the old floor. The near-double bottom at $61,947 gave them a nearby level to define and limit risk, and the rebound has taken the price back to $63,864.

The 100-hour moving average is the next barometer

Drilling down to the hourly chart below, the falling 100-hour moving average (blue line) comes in at $64,273. The price stalled against that moving average on Tuesday and again on Wednesday. If buyers are going to take back more control, they need to get and stay above it.

A sustained break would have traders looking toward the weekend swing highs near $66,069, followed by the falling 200-hour moving average at $66,935. Ultimately, getting and staying above both hourly moving averages would give buyers more control.

As long as the price stays below the 100-hour moving average, sellers remain firmly in control. Another failure there would put the focus back on $61,947 and the broader $61,183 to $62,470 swing area. A move through $61,183 would break the floor buyers have defended twice.

Trading lesson. The floor defines risk. The moving average tests the bounce.

A retest of a prior low gives buyers a level to lean against. Here, a move through $61,947 would weaken the near-double-bottom setup, while a move below $61,183 would break the broader support area. On the topside, watch what happens after the first move above $64,273. If buyers can hold above it, especially on a retest, they will have cleared the level where the last two rallies stalled.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Canada October producer price index +12.6% vs +14.5% y/y prior
item.description:
• Prior was +14.5%
  • Prices for energy and petroleum products increased 1.2% in October, following an 8.6% gain in September
  • Raw materials price index -1.0% vs +4.5% prior
  • Raw materials +23.5% y/y vs +26.6% prior

The raw materials index was led by a 65.6% increase in crude oil, which tells most of the story and that continued in October but the negative reading was driving by lower prices for gold, silver, and platinum group metal ores 

Statistics Canada tracks producer prices through two monthly releases: the Industrial Product Price Index (IPPI) and the Raw Materials Price Index (RMPI). Both are typically published together at 8:30 am ET a few weeks after the reference month ends, and together they serve as Canada’s version of a producer price index for goods.

The IPPI measures prices Canadian manufacturers receive for products as they leave the plant, across a wide range of industries including refined petroleum, lumber and wood products, primary metals, chemicals, food and beverages and motor vehicles. The RMPI measures what manufacturers pay for their key inputs, such as crude oil, metal ores and concentrates, logs, grains, livestock and crude vegetable products. Many of those raw materials are imported or priced off global benchmarks, so the RMPI largely tracks world commodity markets.

Neither index is seasonally adjusted, and both are reported as monthly and annual changes. Because energy carries such a large weight, StatCan also publishes the IPPI excluding energy and petroleum products and the RMPI excluding crude energy products, which give a better sense of broader cost pressures.

The exchange rate plays an outsized role. Many Canadian goods are priced in US dollars, so when the loonie weakens, the Canadian-dollar value of those products rises and lifts the IPPI even if underlying prices haven’t changed. A stronger loonie has the opposite effect.

The reports cover goods only and don’t feed into a central bank target measure, so they rarely move the Canadian dollar or rate expectations. They’re watched mainly as an early signal of cost pressures that could eventually reach consumer prices and as a window on how commodity swings, currency moves and tariffs are affecting Canadian producers.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: US initial jobless claims 203K vs 197K estimate
item.description:
• Initial jobless claims (week ending Nov. 14) — 203,000 vs 197,000 expected. Prior revised to 202,000 from 200,000.
  • Continuing claims (week ending Nov. 7) — 1.763 million vs 1.710 million expected. Prior revised to 1.693 million from 1.697 million.
  • Four-week average of initial claims — 197,750, up from 195,750, revised from 195,250.
  • Four-week average of continuing claims — 1.717 million, up from 1,706,750, revised from 1,707,750.
  • Insured unemployment rate — 1.1%, unchanged.

US initial jobless claims rose by just 1,000 in the week ending November 14, but the result was 5,000 above expectations after the prior week was revised higher. The US Department of Labor released the figures at 8:30 a.m. ET on November 19. dol.gov

The bigger move was in continuing claims, which rose 70,000 in the week ending November 7. That could signal that people already receiving benefits are taking longer to find work. The four-week average also moved higher, while the insured unemployment rate held at 1.1%. Looking at the chart below, the spike higher sticks out but it is off low levels.  

Quick analysis

The report leans softer, with continuing claims carrying more weight than the small rise in new filings. That would normally put some downward pressure on short-term Treasury yields and the US dollar. For the Fed, the question is whether continuing claims keep rising over the next few weeks. Initial claims still averaged fewer than 200,000 over the past four weeks, suggesting layoffs remain relatively limited. dol.gov

What this report measures

Initial claims count new applications for unemployment insurance and offer a timely gauge of layoffs. Continuing claims track ongoing benefit filings and are reported with an extra week’s lag. Traders watch the seasonally adjusted four-week averages to smooth out weekly swings and spot changes in the labor market that could influence Fed policy.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

In the Philly Fed report, prices paid is worth a look given how much of the December debate is about inflation.

In the morning video above, I take a look at the three major currency pairs—EURUSD, USDJPY and GBPUSD—from a technical perspective. For each pair, I outline the bias, the risk-defining levels and the targets that would give either the buyers or sellers more control.

EURUSD. Buyers have the edge above 1.0973

The trading takeaway

An average range tells me how much ground a pair has already covered. At 54% of its average, USDCHF has room to extend in either direction. I’d let a break of 0.8448 or 0.8418 tell me which side is taking control, then watch whether price can hold outside the range. The ability to hold the break is what gives traders a nearby level to lean against.

It's been a very boring session, with very limited news flow and no notable data release. We got a couple of ECB speakers repeating that inflation remains too high and that the central bank is prepared to raise rates further if inflationary pressures persist.

ECB's Moulin warned that inflation remains too high, with elevated oil prices continuing to fuel price pressures. He also stressed that France cannot ignore the reality of its high public debt and budget deficit.

ECB's Nagel expressed confidence that inflation will return to the 2% target and dismissed concerns about a wage-price spiral. He added that an ECB rate hike would send a clear signal, suggesting policymakers remain willing to act if inflationary pressures persist.

The Trump, Xi, Putin meeting concluded with a whole lot of nothing. China, Russia and the US issued a joint statement reaffirming their commitment to strategic stability and international security. The leaders discussed energy security, pledging to increase refined petroleum production and supply, while also calling for limits on the jurisdiction of the ICC and similar institutions. On nuclear issues, they reiterated that nuclear war must never be fought and stressed the importance of continued dialogue to prevent nuclear proliferation.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: Suckers' rally 2.0? Nasdaq rebounds amid Anthropic enthusiasm despite growing macro risks
item.description:
The Nasdaq's suckers' rally, which I discussed in a previous article, eventually erased all the gains and retested the monthly lows. We are now seeing another recovery despite an even more hawkish Fed and no changes in the Middle East tensions.

I think this is another suckers’ rally which is probably being driven by Anthropic enthusiasm. The stock will start trading today on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, although there’s no confirmed opening time.

I would expect a potential rally to fade given no further bullish drivers ahead, and the increasingly high chances of an economic slowdown amid the more hawkish Fed and general deleveraging.

Next week, the most important event will likely be the release of the Flash US PMIs. If the data disappoints, we could see growth concerns intensify and put even more pressure on the Nasdaq. A good report, on the other hand, could trigger a short-term relief rally, but it wouldn’t change much in the bigger picture as it would just give the Fed more confidence to tighten further.

Overall, the outlook for the Nasdaq remains neutral to bearish. We would need an end to the Iran war or a more dovish Fed to get a sustainable bullish trend.  

 

NASDAQ TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME

On the daily chart, we can see the Nasdaq (US100 CFD contract) failed to sustain the break below the major upward trendline again. If we get a pullback into the downward trendline, we can expect the sellers to lean on it, with a defined risk above it, to position for a drop into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to increase the bullish bets into new all-time highs.

NASDAQ TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 4 hour chart, we have a minor upward trendline defining the current recovery. If we get a pullback, we can expect the buyers to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk below it, to keep targeting the major downward trendline. The sellers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking lower to pile in for a drop into new lows.

NASDAQ TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 1 hour chart, we have another minor upward trendline defining the bullish momentum on this timeframe. The buyers will likely continue to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk below it, to keep pushing into new highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break to position for a bigger pullback into the next trendline, targeting a major breakout. The red lines define average daily range for today.

UPCOMING CATALYSTS

Todaywe get the latest US Jobless Claims figures, but the focus will remain on growth concerns amid the more hawkish Fed and the US-Iran developments.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: Solana's downtrend remains intact despite easing selling pressure. What could change the picture?
item.description:
Solana has been recovering some losses as the selling momentum waned amid lack of further bearish catalysts. However, the bearish trend remains intact, with the more hawkish Fed, the US-Iran stalemate and growing concerns about the global growth outlook continuing to weigh on risk sentiment.

There are no major catalysts left for this week. Unless we get some unscheduled geopolitical or macro development, the recovery might extend further.

Next week, the focus will be on the US Flash PMIs given growth concerns. Weak data could exacerbate the negative risk sentiment and put further downward pressure on Solana. Stronger than expected figures, on the other hand, might provide some relief but are unlikely to change the bigger picture.

A more dovish Fed or a breakthrough in the US-Iran situation will likely be needed to reverse the bearish trend.

The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to pile in for a rally into the 125.00 level next.
